sections.h2: Which Jackson County office sends the tax bill?
sections.html:
The Jackson County Tax Collector sends and collects it, using an online portal where a bill can be looked up by tax year. Values come from the Property Appraiser, and the rates come from the County Commission, the School Board and other taxing districts.

The collector's website has a "Due Dates and Discounts" page laid out as a month-by-month calendar. It mixes vehicle, license and property tax items, so the rows below keep only the property ones. A seller can match them against a contract date to see which deadline is next.

The county keeps Central Time, which matters if you pay online near the end of a discount month.

sections.h2: What are the Jackson County property tax months?
sections.html:
The collector's calendar starts collection in November and wants the gross amount by March 31, with a shrinking discount in between.

Property tax rows from the Jackson County Tax Collector Due Dates and Discounts page (jacksontc.com)
MonthCalendar entry
NovemberCollection opens; 4% discount if paid by November 30
December3% discount
January2% discount
February1% discount
MarchGross amount due by March 31
AprilUnpaid real property tax delinquent on April 1; 3% penalty

Business equipment (tangible personal property) follows the same discount months. That row rarely matters to a homeowner, but a landlord or a seller who ran a business from the property should read it.

sections.h2: What does the Jackson County calendar say about delinquent accounts?
sections.html:
After April 1, real property tax carries a 3% penalty on the gross amount. The collector advertises the delinquent list in a local newspaper within 45 days and adds that cost to the bill. During May the list runs weekly for three weeks, ahead of the tax certificate sale. The sale date is set in March, before the delinquency date, so it is knowable early.

A certificate is a lien an investor buys. If it stays unredeemed for two years past the April 1 of issue, the holder may ask for a tax deed, and the clerk auctions the property. For homestead, the statute's opening bid includes one-half of the latest assessed value on top of the amounts due, which is an extra cushion.

Business equipment is handled differently. Unpaid tangible tax grows by 1.5% a month, is advertised within 45 days, and goes to tax warrant processing starting May 1.

sections.h2: Can Jackson County owners spread payments over the year?
sections.html:
Yes. The calendar lists a four-payment plan for the following year's tax, with applications due April 30. Those already enrolled do not reapply.

  • First payment: on or before June 1, but the plan is cancelled if nothing is remitted by June 30.
  • Second payment: before September 30.
  • Third payment: by December 31.
  • Final payment: by March 31.

Two dates in the first item look inconsistent, so call the office to confirm what applies to your account. If you sell while on the plan, give the closing agent a list of paid installments so the proration is right.

sections.h2: Which homestead and assessment limits matter to a Jackson County seller?
sections.html:
A permanent residence on January 1 plus Form DR-501 filed by March 1 opens a homestead exemption of up to $50,000. The first $25,000 touches all taxes, while the second $25,000 applies to value above $50,000 for non-school taxes.

The Save Our Homes cap limits annual growth to 3 percent or inflation, whichever is lower, and the state chart lists 2.7 percent for 2026. Other property is limited to 10 percent a year. A sale ends both limits, which is why a buyer's first bill can exceed the seller's.

  • Age 65 and up: an extra local exemption is possible where an ordinance exists and income fits the limit.
  • Disabled veterans: a $5,000 reduction in assessed value applies at a 10 percent service-connected rating or more.
  • Renting the home or moving out ends homestead.

Ask the Property Appraiser which local ordinances cover your address.

sections.h2: How do I contest a Jackson County value?
sections.html:
Petition the Value Adjustment Board within 25 days after the Property Appraiser mails TRIM notices in August. A denied exemption has a longer window: 30 days from the denial letter.

It pays to begin with an informal talk with the appraiser's staff, since a wrong square footage or exemption status can be fixed without a hearing. Bring a deed, survey or builder's records when the property record itself is wrong.

sections.h2: Does the November 2026 property tax amendment affect a Jackson County bill?
sections.html:
The county announced a town hall on October 13, 2026 about Amendment 3, a property tax proposal on the November 2026 ballot. The notice said the discussion would cover the possible effect on local funding for public safety, fire and emergency services and special districts. It describes the amendment as proposed, so no figures appear.

What changes depends on the ballot result and any law that follows. Check the Florida Department of Revenue and county budget pages for the effective year before relying on a number in a sale. Until new rules are posted, use the dates and amounts on your own bill.

sections.h2: What should a Jackson County seller line up before closing?
sections.html:
Obtain a written payoff from the tax collector and note which year it covers. The title company then splits the current year across buyer and seller. Florida's deed stamp tax is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, and each party named on the deed can be liable.

  • Pull up the account by tax year in the collector's portal to see if older years remain open.
  • Ask about advertising costs and penalties if the account passed April 1.
  • Search the Clerk's records for recorded liens before choosing a closing date.
  • Give the closing agent your installment history.

A cash purchase can be scheduled before a delinquency or certificate sale date, and the title company pays the tax from your proceeds.

faqs.q: When is the last day to pay Jackson County property tax at the gross amount?
faqs.a: March 31. Discounts of 4%, 3%, 2% and 1% apply for payments in November, December, January and February.

faqs.q: What penalty hits an unpaid Jackson County bill on April 1?
faqs.a: Real property gets a 3% penalty on the gross amount. Business equipment gets 1.5% interest per month instead.

faqs.q: When does Jackson County hold its tax certificate sale?
faqs.a: The collector fixes the date in March, ahead of the April 1 delinquency date. Look at the collector's announcements for the exact day.

faqs.q: Does Jackson County allow installment payments?
faqs.a: Yes. Applications for the next year's plan are due April 30, with payments in June, September, December and March. Confirm the June due date with the office.

faqs.q: Will selling raise the next owner's Jackson County bill?
faqs.a: Usually. The sale ends the Save Our Homes cap and the 10 percent limit, and the property resets to just value the next January 1.
